items.title: Natively `print(task)` of a `Task` whose async function never suspends is refused at RUN time ("printing a `Task` is a host object's own inspection"), not at compile time like F25's other host handles — the compile-time refusal fires only when the callee awaits (`sleep(1)`)
items.body: `async fun work(): i32 { 7 }` then `let task = async work(); print(task);` builds natively (the emitter prints `vilan_rt::print(&(task))`) and panics when run; with a `sleep(1)` in `work` the same print is refused at build time by name (`print` of the host handle `Task`). F25's rule (refuse a host handle where it is written) is keyed on the rendered type, which differs for the non-suspending callee. Repro: the find file; `vilan build --backend rust --stdout` builds, `vilan run --backend rust` panics, the JS backend prints node's inspection of the `__Task`. Fix: refuse by the vilan type (`Task<T>`) in `refuse_unprintable`, not the rendered one. Sizing S; vilan-rust's print seam (debug-50 owns the printers; lane left it as it is outside E293).
